content.title: Deep Learning-Based Retinal Vascular Analysis with Quantitative Metrics for Hypertensive Microvascular Damage.
content.abstract: Background/Objectives: The goal of this study was to determine whether deep learning (DL)-assisted retinal vascular analysis detects subclinical microvascular remodeling associated with hypertension-mediated target organ damage (TOD) in patients with absent or mild hypertensive retinopathy (HR). Methods: This prospective study included age-comparable hypertensive patients with TOD (n = 54), hypertensive patients without TOD (n = 54), and healthy controls (n = 54). Color fundus photographs underwent DL-based segmentation using the Retinal Microvascular Health Assessment System, ophthalmologist quality review, and Fiji morphometric analysis. Central retinal arteriolar and venular equivalents (CRAE and CRVE), arteriovenous ratio (AVR), and arterial and venous network metrics were quantified. Results: AVR decreased progressively from 0.814 ± 0.038 in controls to 0.740 ± 0.043 in hypertensive patients without TOD and 0.655 ± 0.042 in those with TOD (p < 0.001). CRAE and CRVE differed among groups (p < 0.001 and p = 0.002). Arterial fractal dimension and vessel area density (VAD) declined stepwise (both p < 0.001), whereas arterial skeletonized vascular density (SVD) and diameter were primarily reduced in TOD. Venous VAD and diameter differed (p = 0.022 and p = 0.006), but venous SVD did not (p = 0.146). After adjustment among hypertensive participants, TOD remained associated with lower AVR, CRAE, and all arterial network metrics except tortuosity (all p < 0.001), but not with venous parameters. Conclusions: Retinal arterial alterations were associated with established extra-retinal TOD in patients with absent or mild HR. Residual cardiovascular confounding limits interpretation, and longitudinal studies are needed to establish temporal relationships, predictive value, and clinical utility.

records.title: Modeling distinct pathogenesis of early- and late-onset preeclampsia via hierarchical representation learning of interactome.

content.title: Modeling distinct pathogenesis of early- and late-onset preeclampsia via hierarchical representation learning of interactome.
content.abstract:
Objectives

We developed and validated the pathogenesis models by hierarchical representation learning of interactomes connecting endometrial maturation, placentation, chorioamnionitis, and hemolysis, elevated liver enzyme, and low platelet (HELLP) syndrome.

Methods

We utilized 19 gene sets from our previous work to infer interactomes to develop (n = 177) and validate (n = 352) explainable artificial intelligence models for each preeclampsia subtype using deep-insight visible neural network, gradient-weighted class activation mapping, and large language model.

Results

The hierarchically learned representations identified novel genes for late-onset preeclampsia (LOPE), similar to chorioamnionitis (ANKRD13A, SLA), and HELLP syndrome (PDE5A). We also identified novel genes for early-onset preeclampsia (EOPE), similar to HELLP syndrome (SWAP70, GREM2, GPR146, PIP5K1B, EZR).

Conclusions

Our pathogenesis models connected HELLP syndrome with both LOPE and EOPE. However, chorioamnionitis was only connected with LOPE.

records.title: The association between large language model dependence and academic anxiety among nursing students: statistical indirect associations through artificial intelligence addiction and academic burnout.

content.title: The association between large language model dependence and academic anxiety among nursing students: statistical indirect associations through artificial intelligence addiction and academic burnout.
content.abstract:
Background

Increasing use of large language models in nursing education has raised questions about the association between reliance on these tools and academic distress. This study examined direct and specific indirect associations between large language model dependence (LMD) and academic anxiety (AA) through artificial intelligence addiction (AIA) and academic burnout (AB).

Methods

A cross-sectional survey was conducted from March to April 2026 among 473 nursing students in Guangdong Province, China, including students undertaking clinical placements. The four constructs were assessed using items selected from published self-report instruments. Partial least squares structural equation modeling was performed with age and sex included as covariates. Direct and specific indirect associations were evaluated using bootstrapping with 5,000 resamples.

Results

Cronbach's α ranged from 0.914 to 0.944, composite reliability from 0.935 to 0.954, and average variance extracted from 0.560 to 0.721. Heterotrait-monotrait ratios ranged from 0.485 to 0.733, supporting discriminant validity. Model fit evidence was mixed: SRMR was 0.068, whereas NFI was 0.812, below the 0.90 reference value. The model explained 49.2% of the variance in academic anxiety. Large language model dependence showed a small positive direct association with academic anxiety (β = 0.138, 95% CI [0.006, 0.278], p = 0.048). Significant specific indirect associations were identified through academic burnout (β = 0.205, 95% CI [0.123, 0.303]) and through artificial intelligence addiction followed by academic burnout (β = 0.098, 95% CI [0.049, 0.147]); both p < 0.001.

Conclusion

Large language model dependence was positively associated with academic anxiety among nursing students, with specific indirect associations through academic burnout and through artificial intelligence addiction followed by academic burnout. These findings highlight the relevance of problematic AI use and study-related exhaustion to academic distress. However, the cross-sectional design does not establish temporal ordering or causal mediation.

records.title: Retinal Artificial Intelligence Reclassifies SCORE2-Based Cardiovascular Risk Across the ESC/EAS Statin-Indication Boundary: A UK Biobank Prospective Cohort Study.

content.title: Retinal Artificial Intelligence Reclassifies SCORE2-Based Cardiovascular Risk Across the ESC/EAS Statin-Indication Boundary: A UK Biobank Prospective Cohort Study.
content.abstract:
Aims

Whether a retinal artificial intelligence (AI) risk score reclassifies SCORE2 cardiovascular risk stratification in statin-naive adults across the ESC/EAS statin-indication boundary is uncertain. We evaluated the retinal AI risk score for 10-year atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease (ASCVD) prediction.

Methods

In 40,672 statin-naive UK Biobank participants (aged 40-69, without diabetes), cardiovascular risk categories and treatment recommendation status (Class I or IIa vs neither) were defined using the 2025 ESC/EAS focused-update framework. Cox models estimated hazard ratios (HRs) adjusted for SCORE2 or for established risk factors. The incremental predictive value of adding the retinal AI risk score to SCORE2 was evaluated using 10-fold cross-validation.

Results

Over a 10.0-year median follow-up (914 ASCVD events), the very high retinal AI risk group independently predicted ASCVD (SCORE2-adjusted HR 2.32 vs low risk; p<0.001). Adding the retinal AI risk score to SCORE2 reclassified risk across the ESC/EAS statin-indication boundary (statin-eligibility NRI [net reclassification improvement] 0.012, p<0.001); reclassification was statistically significant but modest (continuous NRI 0.445, p<0.001), without C-index or net-benefit gain. In the statin-indicated subgroup, retinal AI risk groups further stratified risk (SCORE2-adjusted HR 2.16; p<0.001). Statin-not-indicated participants in the high or very high retinal AI risk groups had numerically similar observed 10-year risk to all statin-indicated, untreated participants (p=0.758). There was no evidence of effect modification by clinically detectable retinal disorder (interaction p=0.93). Incremental value was greater in women than men (sex interaction p<0.001).

Conclusion

Adding the retinal AI risk score to SCORE2 produced modest bidirectional risk reclassification across the ESC/EAS statin-indication boundary; these findings warrant prospective validation.Abstract word count: 250 words.

records.title: Deep Learning-Based Automated Detection, Segmentation, and Quantification of Retinal Fluid on Optical Coherence Tomography: A Validation Study.

content.title: Deep Learning-Based Automated Detection, Segmentation, and Quantification of Retinal Fluid on Optical Coherence Tomography: A Validation Study.
content.abstract: Objectives: To validate a deep learning-based algorithm for automated detection, segmentation, and quantitative assessment of retinal fluid on optical coherence tomography (OCT) across multiple retinal diseases. Methods: In this retrospective validation study, spectral-domain OCT volume scans from eyes with neovascular age-related macular degeneration (nAMD), diabetic macular edema (DME), and macular telangiectasia type 2 (MacTel) were analyzed. Automated segmentation was performed using the fluid analyzer on Skopix by NetraMind Innovations, a deep learning-based framework trained to identify intraretinal fluid (IRF), subretinal fluid (SRF), pigment epithelial detachment (PED), and subretinal hyperreflective material (SHRM). Automated segmentations were reviewed and manually corrected by two masked experienced retina graders, with discrepancies adjudicated by a senior retina specialist. Scan-level detection performance was evaluated using accuracy, sensitivity, specificity, positive predictive value (PPV), negative predictive value (NPV), area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC), and Gwet's first-order agreement coefficient (AC1). Spatial segmentation agreement across all B-scans was assessed using the Dice coefficient. Quantitative agreement between automated and manually corrected fluid volumes was evaluated using correlation and Bland-Altman analyses. Inter-grader reliability was assessed using the intraclass correlation coefficient (ICC). Results: A total of 98 OCT volumes comprising 31 nAMD, 25 DME, and 42 MacTel eyes were included. In nAMD, IRF detection demonstrated a sensitivity of 81.8%, specificity of 83.0%, and AUC of 0.876, while SRF demonstrated a sensitivity of 81.4%, specificity of 96.7%, and AUC of 0.901. In DME, sensitivity, specificity, and AUC were 99.6%, 97.3%, and 0.989 for IRF and 98.4%, 96.4%, and 0.978 for SRF, respectively. In MacTel, IRF demonstrated a sensitivity of 87.3%, specificity of 95.1%, and AUC of 0.927, while SRF demonstrated a sensitivity of 86.8%, specificity of 98.4%, and AUC of 0.929. Segmentation agreement between automated and manually corrected annotations was high across disease groups, with Dice coefficients of 0.829 and 0.922 for IRF and SRF in nAMD, 0.858 and 0.941 in DME, and 0.908 and 0.97 in MacTel, respectively. Automated fluid volumes demonstrated strong correlations with manually corrected measurements, with minimal systematic bias on Bland-Altman analysis. Conclusions: The automated segmentation algorithm demonstrated strong validation performance for the detection and quantitative assessment of retinal fluid across nAMD, DME, and MacTel. High segmentation agreement, particularly for IRF and SRF, and strong volumetric agreement with expert-corrected measurements support the potential use of automated OCT fluid quantification in clinical practice and research.

records.title: Association between deep-learning-derived retinal aging speed and rapid decline of renal function in the Japanese general population.

content.title: Association between deep-learning-derived retinal aging speed and rapid decline of renal function in the Japanese general population.
content.abstract:
Background

The eye and the kidney share microvascular features, and retinal changes have been postulated to reflect systemic cardiometabolic dysfunction. Recently, retinal age, estimated by deep learning (DL) from a single fundus photograph, has been shown to predict cardiovascular events. The present study aimed to determine whether retinal aging speed, defined as the individual-specific annual rate of change in DL-estimated retinal age, is associated with rapid estimated glomerular filtration rate (eGFR) decline.

Methods

We retrospectively analyzed the longitudinal data obtained from 7807 Japanese individuals who underwent repeated health check-ups with serial measurements of eGFR and fundus photographs (median 9.0 visits over median 8.0 years). We evaluated the relationship between retinal aging speed during the baseline period (from baseline to year 4) and rapid eGFR decline (≤ -3 ml/min/1.73 m²/year) during the follow-up period (after year 4).

Results

The incidence of rapid eGFR decline was significantly higher in the highest quartile of retinal aging speed than in the lowest quartile as the reference group in the fully adjusted model adjusting age, sex, body mass index, blood pressure, diabetes, smoking, eGFR, and proteinuria [odds ratio (OR) 1.34; 95% confidence interval (CI) 1.06-1.68; P = .015]. In the multivariable logistic regression models, retinal aging speed was associated with rapid eGFR decline after adjusting multiple key confounders (OR 1.14; 95% CI 1.02-1.29; P = .027).

Conclusions

Taken together, DL-derived retinal aging speed is independently associated with rapid eGFR decline in the Japanese general population.

records.title: Global research trends of artificial intelligence in echocardiography (1984-2025): a bibliometric analysis.

content.title: Global research trends of artificial intelligence in echocardiography (1984-2025): a bibliometric analysis.
content.abstract:
Background

Echocardiography has evolved substantially since its introduction in 1954. Artificial intelligence (AI) offers transformative potential for image acquisition, quantification, interpretation, and reporting. Despite growing research interest, a comprehensive evaluation of the historical trends and evolution of AI in echocardiography is lacking. The study aimed to conduct a comprehensive bibliometric analysis of the global research landscape in this field.

Methods

A systematic literature search was conducted using the Scopus and Web of Science Core Collection databases for publications on AI in echocardiography from inception through November 10, 2025; no language filter was applied. Data analysis was performed using Microsoft Excel, Microsoft Access, and IBM SPSS Statistics. In addition, bibliometric mapping and data visualization were conducted.

Results

Overall, 2682 publications received 35,083 citations (mean, 13.08 citations per publication), spanning 1984-2025. Original articles, conference papers, and review articles accounted for 87.4% and 98.5% of total publications and citations, respectively. Publication output remained limited until approximately 2015, rose gradually thereafter, and accelerated markedly after 2018, with similar output in 2024 and 2025. The United States led in both publication volume and total citations, followed by China and the United Kingdom. The United States also had the highest collaboration link strength, and seven of the top 10 institutions were in North America (six in the United States and one in Canada). Mayo Clinic ranked first, with 142 publications and 3604 citations, and had the earliest first indexed publication among the top institutions (1992). The journal JACC: Cardiovascular Imaging ranked first in both total citations (1,911) and citations per publication (36.75). "Echocardiography," "deep learning," "artificial intelligence," and "machine learning" were the most frequently used terms. The thematic evolution showed continuity of algorithmic-centric themes (1984-2019) with emerging clinically oriented themes (2020-2025).

Conclusions

This comprehensive bibliometric analysis highlights the rapid expansion of AI research in echocardiography, characterized by an accelerating publication output and emerging clinically oriented research topics. These findings reflect growing research interest in integrating AI into echocardiographic practice and highlight the need for future research prioritizing multicenter validation, clinical translation, and equitable real-world implementation.

records.title: Beyond scales: Artificial intelligence, language, and behavior in suicide risk modeling-a narrative review.
records.publisher: European neuropsychopharmacology : the journal of the European College of Neuropsychopharmacology

content.title: Beyond scales: Artificial intelligence, language, and behavior in suicide risk modeling-a narrative review.
content.abstract: Suicide is a leading, preventable cause of premature mortality, yet identifying individuals at imminent risk remains difficult. There are no validated biomarkers for routine stratification, and common approaches (clinical interviews, rating scales, self-report) are limited by subjectivity, reporting bias, and weak positive predictive value for rare outcomes. Rapid advances in artificial intelligence (AI)-including machine learning, deep learning, and large language models-offer opportunities to integrate heterogeneous signals relevant to risk and treatment response. This narrative review summarizes recent AI-enabled prediction and characterization of suicidal thoughts and behaviors across major data modalities: structured electronic health records and claims; natural language processing of clinical notes and digital text; speech and facial/behavioral signals; neuroimaging and other neurobiological measures; and passive sensing from smartphones and wearables. We review common modeling and evaluation practices, emphasizing clinically relevant performance assessment (discrimination and calibration) and the importance of temporal and external validation. We also highlight barriers to translation, including class imbalance and label noise, dataset shift across sites and time, limited prospective evaluation, and the need for interpretable outputs that can support medication decisions and care pathways (e.g., triage, monitoring, and stepped interventions). Ethical and implementation challenges-privacy and consent, algorithmic bias and equity, governance, and the clinical consequences of false-positive and false-negative predictions-are discussed with an emphasis on safe deployment. We conclude with priorities for the field, including multimodal longitudinal cohorts, harmonized reporting standards, and pragmatic trials to determine whether AI decision support measurably improves suicide-prevention outcomes.

records.title: Application of an Artificial Intelligence Simulated Patient Model in Teaching Neurosurgical Decision-Making.

content.title: Application of an Artificial Intelligence Simulated Patient Model in Teaching Neurosurgical Decision-Making.
content.abstract:
Aim

Training in neurosurgical decision-making remains a challenging component of standardized residency training. Traditional teaching models are limited in their ability to simulate the uncertainty and complexity encountered in real-world clinical scenarios. As a novel educational tool, the potential value of artificial intelligence (AI)-simulated patient models in surgical decision-making training requires further evaluation. This study aimed to explore the application of an AI-simulated patient model in neurosurgical decision-making education and to assess its effectiveness in improving residents' clinical decision-making abilities.

Methods

A retrospective study was conducted involving 157 residents who underwent standardized residency training in the Department of Neurosurgery from January 2023 to April 2026. Based on the implementation of the AI-simulated teaching model beginning in January 2025, participants were divided into two groups according to the teaching model used: an experimental group (n = 72, receiving AI-simulated patient teaching from January 2025 to April 2026) and a control group (n = 85, receiving traditional case discussion teaching from January 2023 to December 2024). The experimental group used a large language model-based virtual patient system powered by DeepSeek to perform dialogue-driven history taking, image interpretation, surgical planning, and risk prediction with real-time feedback, while the control group received conventional methods. After teaching, an objective structured clinical examination (OSCE) was used to assess surgical decision-making across five dimensions, including localization diagnosis, surgical approach, risk identification, emergency management, and surgical timing, and a questionnaire was used to measure teaching satisfaction.

Results

The total score for surgical decision-making ability was significantly higher in the experimental group than in the control group (p < 0.001). Dimensional analysis showed that localization diagnosis, surgical method selection, risk identification, emergency response, and surgical timing judgment were higher in the experimental group than in the control group (all p < 0.05). The excellent rate for each assessment dimension (>85 points) was significantly higher in the experimental group than in the control group (p < 0.05). The satisfaction score was also higher in the experimental group than in the control group (p < 0.001).

Conclusions

The AI-simulated patient model based on a general-purpose large language model was associated with better surgical decision-making performance among neurosurgery residents. It has significant advantages in localization diagnosis, surgical approach selection, risk identification, emergency response, and judgment of surgical timing, and is well accepted by residents.

records.title: Impact of Image Bit Depth Reduction on Deep Learning Performance in Chest Radiograph Analysis: A Multi-institutional Study.

content.title: Impact of Image Bit Depth Reduction on Deep Learning Performance in Chest Radiograph Analysis: A Multi-institutional Study.
content.abstract:
Rationale and objectives

Medical imaging typically generates 12-bit to 16-bit formats, yet conversion to 8-bit is often required. While deep learning has been widely explored in medical imaging, the influence of image bit depth on model performance is not fully understood. This study evaluates the impact of conversion from 16-bit to 8-bit for sex, age, and obesity classification using deep learning.

Materials and methods

In this retrospective, multi-institutional study, we analyzed 100,002 chest radiographs from 48,047 participants across three institutions. Images were uniformly quantized from the fixed 0-65535 range to 256 levels (0-255) with no additional processing. Three convolutional neural network architectures (ResNet52, EfficientNetB2, and ConvNeXtSmall) were trained on both 16-bit and 8-bit versions of the images. Model performance was evaluated using internal test datasets, randomly split multiple times, and an external test dataset. Statistical analysis included paired comparisons of area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC-ROC) values, with Bonferroni correction for multiple comparisons.

Results

Across all architectures and classification tasks, differences between 16-bit and 8-bit model performance were minimal (mean differences ranging from -0.218%-0.184%). Statistical analyses revealed no significant differences in AUC-ROC values between bit depths for any model-task combination (all p values > 0.05 after Bonferroni correction). Effect sizes were small to moderate (Cohen's d ranging from -0.415-0.391).

Conclusion

No statistically significant differences were detected between models trained on 16-bit and 8-bit images in the three evaluated tasks. These findings suggest that conversion to 8-bit images may reduce data storage requirements and improve data processing efficiency. Further research is needed to assess their usefulness in clinical tasks.

records.title: Artificial Intelligence in Breast Cancer Diagnosis, Treatment, and Perioperative Management: A Systematic Review of Current Applications and Future Perspectives.

content.title: Artificial Intelligence in Breast Cancer Diagnosis, Treatment, and Perioperative Management: A Systematic Review of Current Applications and Future Perspectives.
content.abstract:
Background

Breast cancer is the most frequently diagnosed malignancy in women globally, accounting for approximately 2.30 million new cases and 666,103 deaths in 2022. Artificial intelligence technologies including machine learning, deep learning, radiomics, and natural language processing have been widely applied across the breast cancer care continuum. However, no systematic review restricted to primary studies with patient-level or image-level data has synthesized evidence spanning all clinical domains simultaneously.

Objectives

To evaluate the performance, methodological quality, and clinical relevance of artificial intelligence primary studies across screening and diagnostic imaging, digital pathology, radiomics, perioperative management, prognostic prediction, and natural language processing in breast cancer.

Methods

PubMed/MEDLINE, Scopus, Web of Science, Embase, and the Cochrane Library were searched from January 2015 to May 2026. Eligibility was restricted to original primary research reporting patient-level or image-level data; secondary syntheses were explicitly excluded. Risk of bias was assessed using QUADAS-2 and PROBAST. Reporting followed PRISMA 2020 guidelines.

Results

Of 5,275 identified records, 17 primary studies met eligibility criteria. In screening mammography (seven studies; n = 7,540 to 144,231 examinations), deep learning achieved area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC) values of 0.876 to 0.939; a randomised trial in 80,033 women demonstrated non-inferiority to double reading with a 44.3% reduction in radiologist workload. In digital pathology (five studies; 270 to 44,732 whole-slide images), deep learning achieved AUC 0.985 to 0.994, exceeding unassisted pathologist performance in lymph node metastasis detection. Magnetic resonance imaging radiomics predicted pathological complete response in HER2-positive breast cancer with AUC 0.80. No breast cancer-specific perioperative primary study met the eligibility criteria. Deep survival networks achieved concordance index 0.626 versus 0.612 for Cox regression in breast cancer cohorts. Natural language processing identified metastatic recurrence in breast cancer clinical records with sensitivity 83% and specificity 73%. Risk of bias was low to moderate for imaging and pathology studies and high for small sample radiomics studies. Density-stratified performance was reported by only two imaging studies, and receptor status prediction from haematoxylin and eosin staining had not been validated as a safe alternative to immunohistochemistry.

Conclusions

Artificial intelligence demonstrated clinically meaningful performance across the five domains with eligible primary studies. Breast cancer-specific perioperative and intensive care primary studies were absent, representing the largest evidence gap. External validation, demographic diversity, and prospective clinical integration evidence remained the most consistently identified limitations. Prediction of molecular receptor status without immunohistochemistry requires rigorous prospective safety validation before it can complement standard testing.

records.title: Digital twin oncology and multi-omics-driven artificial intelligence models for personalized drug response prediction: A systematic survey of emerging computational paradigms and clinical implementation challenges.

content.title: Digital twin oncology and multi-omics-driven artificial intelligence models for personalized drug response prediction: A systematic survey of emerging computational paradigms and clinical implementation challenges.
content.abstract: The increasing complexity of tumor heterogeneity and variable therapeutic response has intensified the need for accurate personalized drug response prediction in oncology. Traditional trial-and-error chemotherapy strategies often result in suboptimal outcomes, toxicity, and delayed therapeutic adjustments. Rapid advances in multi-omics technologies, artificial intelligence (AI) and digital twin modeling have significantly reshaped computational oncology research. This survey systematically reviews peer-reviewed research and review articles published from 2021 onward that investigate emerging computational paradigms integrating digital twins and multi-omics AI for drug response prediction. The foundational concepts in digital twin oncology, multi-omics profiling and AI-driven precision medicine are outlined initially. The existing approaches are categorized into four major paradigms such as omics-driven machine learning models, deep learning based multimodal architectures, mechanistic digital twin simulation frameworks and hybrid digital twin AI systems enabling adaptive therapy optimization. The multi-omics data integration strategies, including early, intermediate, late, network-based and graph/pathway-based fusion techniques. The survey synthesizes recent developments in drug sensitivity prediction, immunotherapy response modeling, tumor evolution forecasting and virtual clinical trials, while critically analyzing challenges related to data heterogeneity, interpretability, generalization, privacy, regulatory compliance and ethical considerations. Finally, future directions are highlighted such as real-time adaptive digital twins, federated learning, explainable AI and regulatory ready clinical deployment frameworks. Overall, this review provides a structured taxonomy, comparative analysis and research roadmap for advancing integrated digital twin and multi omics AI systems toward clinically actionable precision oncology.

records.title: Is Large Language Model a New Hope for the Global South? A Rapid Bibliometric Synthesis of Artificial Intelligence in Anatomy Education.

content.title: Is Large Language Model a New Hope for the Global South? A Rapid Bibliometric Synthesis of Artificial Intelligence in Anatomy Education.
content.abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI), especially the recent proliferation of generative Large Language Models (LLMs), is transforming traditional anatomy education by introducing new teaching tools. However, the adoption of these cutting-edge technologies raises questions about global educational equity. It remains unclear whether AI will serve as a digital equalizer or further exacerbate marginalization. This rapid bibliometric synthesis aims to provide a comprehensive, data-driven overview of the "Application of Artificial Intelligence in Anatomy Education" (AAAE). We seek to map the intellectual landscape, detect structural and technological shifts, evaluate the geopolitical disparities, and provide corresponding references. A total of 85 consolidated records were retrieved from Web of Science and Scopus. These data constituted the whole panorama of AAAE. Bibliometrix and CiteSpace were utilized for static and dynamic mapping. A multidisciplinary expert panel validated the thematic clusters using Gwet's AC1 and the Normalized Herfindahl-Hirschman Index (HHI). Publications surged following ChatGPT's release, indicating a shift from specialized computer vision to the application of general-purpose LLMs. While high-income countries maintain leadership, AI could exert a "democratizing effect" on upper-middle-income countries, doubling their odds of publication compared to traditional anatomy. Six research frontiers and three research trajectories were captured, and corresponding implications for future researchers in the global south and north were presented. AAAE could be conducted using a stratified strategy: different expansions of AI technologies for pedagogy; leveraging commercial APIs to bypass infrastructure bottlenecks; and validating open-source models. Global equity critically demands cross-border collaboration and inclusive datasets.

records.title: Artificial intelligence analysis of oral mucosal lesions in white-light clinical photographs: A systematic review of visual features and validation.

content.title: Artificial intelligence analysis of oral mucosal lesions in white-light clinical photographs: A systematic review of visual features and validation.
content.abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) is increasingly applied to conventional oral photographs for recognition, classification, localization, segmentation, and risk assessment of oral mucosal lesions. This systematic review evaluated how clinically relevant visual information-including color, texture, morphology, borders, and spatial patterns-is represented by AI systems and assessed performance, validation, explainability, human comparison, and clinical translation. PubMed, Embase, Scopus, and Google Scholar were searched for studies directly analyzing conventional white-light clinical photographs. Risk of bias was assessed with PROBAST + AI, and certainty with Grading of Recommendations Assessment, Development, and Evaluation-based approaches. Fifty-three studies were included, 30 published in 2025-2026. Forty-six used implicit deep-learning visual representations, three multimodal vision-language models, two explicit color analyses, and two explicit texture analyses. Thirty-one studies primarily addressed image-level diagnostic classification/recognition, 15 spatial detection/localization or lesion delineation, six screening/triage/referral or biopsy-oriented decision support, and one longitudinal malignant-transformation prediction. Six used independent external cohorts and five compared AI with human readers. Methodological concerns were frequent, no sufficiently coherent group supported meta-analysis, and certainty remained limited across evidence bodies. Current evidence therefore supports technical feasibility rather than established clinical effectiveness, with translation requiring stronger patient-level independence, external validation, prospective multicenter evaluation, and evidence of clinical benefit.

records.title: Artificial Intelligence in Pulmonary Hypertension: Advancements, Opportunities, and Challenges.

content.title: Artificial Intelligence in Pulmonary Hypertension: Advancements, Opportunities, and Challenges.
content.abstract: Pulmonary hypertension (PH) is a progressive cardiopulmonary disorder associated with high morbidity and mortality. Delayed diagnosis, heterogeneous disease phenotypes, and variable treatment responses remain major clinical challenges. Artificial intelligence (AI), including machine learning and deep learning, has emerged as a promising tool for improving PH management. AI-based models have demonstrated promising performance in screening, diagnosis, classification, risk stratification, and prognosis prediction using multimodal data such as electrocardiography, chest radiography, computed tomography, cardiac magnetic resonance imaging, echocardiography, and electronic health records. Furthermore, AI may support individualized risk assessment, treatment-response prediction, early identification of right ventricular deterioration, and longitudinal remote monitoring. Emerging technologies, including explainable AI, federated learning, large language models, and digital twins, may further advance precision medicine in PH. Despite these advances, data quality, interpretability, privacy, and clinical implementation of AI remain challenges. This review summarizes current applications, opportunities, and challenges of AI in PH and discusses future directions for AI-assisted precision healthcare.

records.title: Medication adherence and influencing factors in children and adolescents with attention deficit hyperactivity disorder (ADHD): a systematic review and meta-analysis.

content.title: Medication adherence and influencing factors in children and adolescents with attention deficit hyperactivity disorder (ADHD): a systematic review and meta-analysis.
content.abstract:
Background

Medication non-adherence is widely occurring in children and adolescents with ADHD, which may lead to adverse consequences. However, the pooled adherence rate and influencing factors are inconsistent in different studies.

Methods

We searched PubMed, Embase (Ovid), Cochrane Library, and four Chinese Databases from inception to 20 February 2024. All types of studies were included. Two researchers independently extracted data and assessed the risk of bias based on ROBINS-I, NOS, and AHRQ. A random-effects meta-analysis was conducted to pool the prevalence estimates and factors that can be combined.

Results

After screening 2,360 publications, 63 studies were finally included, involving 450,759 participants. The general quality of the included studies was moderate to high quality. Adherence rates were reported in 50 studies, and a pooled adherence rate was 43.6% (95% Confidence Interval [CI] 39.0%-48.3%). The sensitivity analysis shows robust study results. However, both the primary analysis and the sensitivity analysis indicated high heterogeneity. The results of Meta-analysis identified five factors influencing adherence, of which female (Odds Ratio [OR] = 1.07, 95%CI:1.03-1.11), fewer medication doses (OR = 0.45, 95%CI:0.27-0.75), parental agreement with the medication plan (OR = 1.87, 95%CI:1.16-3.02), single-child families (OR = 1.80, 95%CI:1.29-2.52), and medication education for parents (OR = 6.34, 95%CI:3.97-10.12) can improve medication adherence. Besides, we also identified seven factors influencing adherence by qualitative analysis.

Conclusion

Medication adherence is challenging for children and adolescents with ADHD, moreover, the meta-analysis of adherence rates showed high heterogeneity. We identified five modifiable factors by meta-analysis that are related to medication adherence, while other factors require further research.

Systematic review registration

identifier CRD42024514310.

records.title: The impact of artificial intelligence on periodontal disease detection and treatment.

content.title: The impact of artificial intelligence on periodontal disease detection and treatment.
content.abstract: Periodontal disease (PD) is one of the most prevalent chronic inflammatory non-comunicable diseases worldwide. Early diagnosis and timely intervention for periodontitis are essential to prevent the onset and progression of the disease, especially due to the associated risk, sometimes subclinical, of negative correlations with various systemic diseases that impair quality of life. In this regard, artificial intelligence (AI) has emerged as a transformative tool in healthcare, and its application in the detection and treatment of periodontal disease holds considerable promise. This study aims to review and update the latest evidence on the role of AI in the diagnosis and management of periodontal disease, emphasising advancements in machine learning (ML) algorithms, diagnostic imaging, and predictive modelling. Moreover, it is analyzed how AI-driven technologies, such as deep learning models applied to radiographs and clinical data, can enhance diagnostic accuracy, predict disease progression, and assist in personalized treatment planning. The potential of AI to optimise clinical workflows and improve patient outcomes is also discussed, alongside the challenges of integrating it into routine dental practice, including ethical considerations and data privacy concerns. This review highlights the current state of AI in periodontology, identifies key research gaps, and offers recommendations for future directions in AI-driven periodontal care.

records.title: Standardized Clinical Photography for Improving Dermatological Treatment Adherence (Scoping Review): Evidence Landscape and Research Gaps.

content.title: Standardized Clinical Photography for Improving Dermatological Treatment Adherence (Scoping Review): Evidence Landscape and Research Gaps.
content.abstract: Treatment adherence remains suboptimal across chronic dermatological conditions, contributing to poor clinical outcomes and increased healthcare burden. Despite the established role of standardized clinical photography in clinical documentation, its specific application as an adherence-promoting intervention remains poorly characterized. This scoping review aimed to systematically map the literature on photographic feedback in dermatology, identify research gaps, and propose methodological recommendations for future randomized controlled trials (RCTs). We conducted a scoping review according to the Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses extension for Scoping Reviews (PRISMA-ScR). Systematic searches of PubMed, Embase, Cochrane Library, and Web of Science, supplemented by Europe PMC, ClinicalTrials.gov, WHO ICTRP, and Google Scholar (first 200 records), were performed from database inception to December 31, 2025 (searches executed September 20-27, 2026). Of 1181 identified records, 18 studies met the eligibility criteria: five provided direct evidence, five indirect evidence, and eight methodological evidence. Direct evidence comprised three observational studies in hair loss disorders encompassing 3,218 patients (93% of participants derived from a single retrospective cohort), one virtual feasibility study in atopic dermatitis, and one remote photographic wound-monitoring study in keloids; the remaining five prespecified conditions (psoriasis, acne, vitiligo, rosacea, and melasma) yielded zero direct evidence, although vitiligo has an established methodological photography literature. Of the five direct-evidence studies, four measured motivation, satisfaction, task completion, or image-upload compliance rather than treatment adherence per se. Indirect evidence from smartphone applications exists for psoriasis and atopic dermatitis, but these bundle photography with other digital functions. We propose the "early difference refutation" design to address reverse causality in future RCTs. High-quality RCTs are urgently needed to determine whether photographic feedback alone can improve dermatological treatment adherence.

records.title: Artificial intelligence-based chatbots to enhance medication adherence among patients with non-communicable chronic diseases: Systematic review and meta-analysis.

content.title: Artificial intelligence-based chatbots to enhance medication adherence among patients with non-communicable chronic diseases: Systematic review and meta-analysis.
content.abstract: Medication adherence remains a major public health challenge among patients with non-communicable diseases (NCDs) worldwide. Artificial intelligence (AI)-based chatbots may enhance adherence by automating reminders, education, and real-time support. This systematic review and meta-analysis evaluated the effectiveness of AI-based chatbots in improving medication adherence among patients with NCDs. This review (CRD420251151031) is reported in accordance with the PRISMA guidelines. Relevant studies were identified from PubMed, MEDLINE, Embase, Web of Science, Global Health, CINAHL, Cochrane Library, APA PsycINFO, and APA PsycArticles up to August 2025. Eligible designs included randomized controlled trials (RCTs), quasi-experimental studies, and single-arm pre-post studies. Seven studies published between 2017 and 2025 were included, of which six RCTs contributed to the meta-analysis. The pooled standardized mean difference (SMD) for medication adherence was 0.69 (95% confidence interval: 0.17 to 1.22; p = 0.01), indicating a significant medium effect with high heterogeneity (I2 = 97%). Subgroup analyses revealed greater effects for cardiovascular diseases and short-term interventions (<6 months). Daily and weekly to monthly interventions were effective, whereas on-demand or episodic interventions were not. Significant improvements were also observed when adherence was assessed using self-reported measures or pill counts. AI-based chatbots that incorporated three functions (medication reminders, education and health coaching, and real-time question-answer features) showed significant improvement in medication adherence, whereas those with dual functions did not. These findings indicate that AI-based chatbots significantly improve medication adherence in NCDs. Chatbots have the potential to supplement existing interventions to support medication adherence.

records.title: Barriers and Facilitators to Patient Acceptance of Artificial Intelligence in Health Care: Systematic Review.

content.title: Barriers and Facilitators to Patient Acceptance of Artificial Intelligence in Health Care: Systematic Review.
content.abstract:
Background

Artificial intelligence (AI) in the domain of health care is increasing in prominence. Acceptance is an indispensable prerequisite for the widespread implementation of AI.

Objective

This study aimed to explore barriers and facilitators influencing patients' acceptance of AI.

Methods

We conducted a systematic review following PRISMA (Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses) guidelines. Nine databases, including PubMed, Web of Science, and Embase, were comprehensively searched from inception to December 23, 2025. We included qualitative, quantitative, and mixed methods studies investigating adult patients' attitudes toward medical AI. Two researchers independently screened records, extracted data, and appraised methodological quality using the Mixed Methods Appraisal Tool. Following the Joanna Briggs Institute convergent integrated approach, data synthesis was guided by integrating the Unified Theory of Acceptance and Use of Technology 2 (UTAUT2) and the Theoretical Domains Framework (TDF). Factors were mapped to behavior change techniques (BCTs) and evaluated for practical feasibility using the Affordability, Practicability, Effectiveness and cost-effectiveness, Acceptability, Side-effects/safety, and Equity criteria.

Results

A total of 61 studies met the inclusion criteria out of 7452 search results. Study designs included qualitative (n=20), quantitative (n=35), and mixed methods (n=6). Performance and effort expectancies were the primary determinants of acceptance. Major barriers comprised perceived operational complexity, lack of algorithmic trust, reduced interpersonal interaction, privacy vulnerabilities, and high costs. Facilitators included transparent data governance, interpretability of AI decisions, improved clinician-patient communication, and human-centered design. Education level and disease severity emerged as key moderating variables. Through UTAUT2-TDF mapping, we identified 25 distinct BCTs (6 high, 14 medium, and 5 low feasibility) and formulated 40 actionable intervention strategies.

Conclusions

This study innovatively integrates the UTAUT2 and TDF frameworks to evaluate patient acceptance of medical AI. Unlike existing reviews that predominantly evaluate isolated psychosocial factors or purely technical attributes, this transtheoretical approach differentiates itself by merging technology adoption mechanisms directly with behavioral drivers. Consequently, it contributes to the field by systematically identifying multilevel factors influencing acceptance, including performance expectancy, effort expectancy, and ethical security, and translating these into 40 actionable BCTs. In real-world clinical practice, these findings provide a feasible, prioritized blueprint for clinicians and administrators to design patient-centered interventions, enhancing the clinical integration and long-term effectiveness of medical AI.

records.title: Effectiveness of acupuncture for cancer-related fatigue: a systematic reviews and meta-analysis.

content.title: Effectiveness of acupuncture for cancer-related fatigue: a systematic reviews and meta-analysis.
content.abstract:
Background/objectives

Acupuncture is recommended for the treatment of cancer-related fatigue (CRF), but the strength of evidence remains limited. This study aims to comprehensively update the evaluation of the effectiveness of acupuncture for CRF and clarify the latest strength of evidence.

Methods

Eight databases were searched from inception to April 2025 to identify eligible randomized controlled trials (RCTs). The quality of the study was assessed using the Cochrane risk of bias tool version 2.0(ROB 2.0). Meta-analyses were performed using R studio 4.4 software and RevMan software (version 5.4). Subgroup analyses by acupuncture type were conducted to explore sources of heterogeneity and further elucidate the efficacy of different acupuncture modalities. Publication bias was assessed when applicable. Finally, evidence quality was rated using the GRADE system.

Results

This meta-analysis included 28 RCTs. Risk of bias assessment indicated low overall study quality. The meta-analysis of the primary outcome(Piper Fatigue Scale, PFS) revealed that acupuncture intervention significantly improved fatigue levels compared to the control group (MD = -0.56, 95% CI: -0.74 to -0.38, I2 = 45%, P < 0.01). Subgroup analyses showed that different acupuncture type had distinct advantages, suggesting distinct targeted advantages. Other factors showed significant differences. Sensitivity analyses for multiple outcome measures yielded unstable results, with indications of publication bias. According to GRADE criteria, the most outcomes were rated as low or very low quality.

Conclusions

Current evidence suggests that acupuncture may alleviate CRF. However, conclusive evidence supporting its therapeutic efficacy remains limited. Given the methodological concerns and low certainty of the available evidence, further high-quality studies are needed to confirm these findings.

Systematic review registration

https://www.crd.york.ac.uk/prospero/, identifier CRD42024603184.

records.title: Deep learning in lower gastrointestinal cancer detection: Advances in endoscopic, radiologic, and histopathologic diagnostics.

content.title: Deep learning in lower gastrointestinal cancer detection: Advances in endoscopic, radiologic, and histopathologic diagnostics.
content.abstract: Gastrointestinal (GI) cancers, particularly colorectal cancer, continue to be a major contributor to global cancer-related morbidity and mortality. Despite significant advancements in screening protocols and treatment strategies, early detection remains a clinical challenge due to the limitations of conventional diagnostic tools, which often suffer from inter-observer variability, limited sensitivity, and time-intensive procedures. In recent years the integration of artificial intelligence (AI), especially deep learning (DL) techniques, into medical diagnostics has opened new frontiers for enhancing detection accuracy, speed, and consistency across clinical domains. This review explores the transformative impact of DL-based AI models in detecting lower GI cancers, focusing on three key diagnostic modalities: Endoscopy; radiology; and histopathology. In endoscopic practice convolutional neural networks are used to detect and classify colorectal polyps in real-time, significantly reducing miss rates and aiding non-specialist endoscopists in decision-making. In radiology DL algorithms trained on computed tomography and magnetic resonance imaging data are valuable for automated lesion detection, segmentation, and staging, often outperforming conventional imaging. Histopathological analysis, traditionally reliant on manual examination, is now accelerated by DL models capable of processing whole-slide images to identify architectural distortions and cellular anomalies with high reproducibility and diagnostic accuracy. This review evaluates DL model performance, including sensitivity, specificity, and area under the curve and addresses technical and ethical challenges, including dataset diversity, interpretability, and integration into healthcare workflows. Ultimately, the convergence of AI and clinical medicine has the potential to improve diagnostic outcomes and personalized care for patients with lower GI cancers.

records.title: Inflammation-mediated effects of diabetes mellitus on male fertility: a systematic review and meta-analysis.

content.title: Inflammation-mediated effects of diabetes mellitus on male fertility: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
content.abstract:
Background

Diabetes mellitus (DM) has emerged as a rapidly growing global health problem, imposing substantial socioeconomic burdens and multidimensional health consequences, including adverse effects on male fertility. Although accumulating evidence suggests associations between DM and male reproductive dysfunction, comprehensive mechanistic insights, particularly through inflammatory pathways, remain inadequately elucidated.

Method

We conducted a systematic literature search on Web of Science, Embase, and PubMed databases (1972-2022) to investigate DM-related male infertility through meta-analysis. Following PRISMA guidelines, eight of 168 studies on type 1 diabetes (T1D) and nine of 185 studies on type 2 diabetes (T2D) were included to screen the relationship between diabetes and male infertility. In addition, 10 of 840 inflammation-related studies (1961-2022) underwent rigorous selection for mechanistic exploration. Meta-analysis was conducted to evaluate the summary relative risk (RR) and 95% confidence intervals (CIs) across the combined studies.

Results

Meta-analysis demonstrated a significant impairment of male fertility in diabetic populations. Subgroup analyses revealed that T2D is more likely to cause male infertility compared to T1D. Despite low between-study heterogeneity, inflammation biomarkers (e.g., TNF-α) were implicated in diabetes-induced male infertility. Transcriptomic analyses further identified enriched inflammatory pathways and altered expression of fertility-related genes.

Conclusion

Current evidence indicates that diabetes adversely affects male fertility through inflammatory pathways.

records.title: Elevated Epicardial Adipose Tissue and Ischemic Stroke Risk: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.

content.title: Elevated Epicardial Adipose Tissue and Ischemic Stroke Risk: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.
content.abstract: Introduction: Epicardial adipose tissue (EAT), a fat depot between the myocardium and pericardium, produces pro-inflammatory adipokines, contributing to inflammation, insulin resistance, and endothelial dysfunction. EAT has been recognized as an independent risk factor for cardiovascular diseases, including atrial fibrillation (AFib) and acute ischemic stroke (AIS). This study explores the association between EAT and AIS risk, with a focus on populations with cardiovascular comorbidities. Material and Methods: This meta-analysis adhered to MOOSE and PRISMA guidelines. A comprehensive search of PubMed, SCOPUS, and Embase databases was conducted, targeting studies evaluating the association between EAT and AIS. Inclusion criteria encompassed RCTs, cohort, case-control, and cross-sectional studies. Quality assessment was performed using appropriate tools, and statistical analysis involved pooled odds ratios (ORs) with 95% confidence intervals (CIs) using a binary random-effects model. Results: The search identified 711 studies, eight of which met the inclusion criteria, yielding 7412 participants. Analysis revealed that increased EAT thickness significantly correlated with higher odds of AIS (aOR: 3.60 [2.26-5.74], I2 = 74.24%). Sensitivity analysis confirmed the robustness of these findings despite publication bias. Higher epicardial adipose volume was also associated with an increased AIS risk (aOR: 1.17 [1.03-1.34], I2 = 49.54%). Conclusions: Increased EAT thickness and volume are associated with a higher risk of AIS in populations with cardiovascular comorbidities, including AFib. EAT's pro-inflammatory and pro-thrombotic properties may contribute to stroke pathophysiology. These findings highlight the potential utility of EAT measurement in stroke risk stratification and support further research to integrate EAT assessment into clinical practice.

records.title: Comparative efficacy and safety of pharmacological treatments for lower-risk myelodysplastic syndromes: a Systematic Review and network meta-analysis.

content.title: Comparative efficacy and safety of pharmacological treatments for lower-risk myelodysplastic syndromes: a Systematic Review and network meta-analysis.
content.abstract:
Background

The comparative efficacy of pharmacological treatments for lower-risk myelodysplastic syndromes (LR-MDS) remains uncertain because head-to-head randomised evidence is limited.

Methods

We performed a systematic review and network meta-analysis of randomised controlled trials evaluating pharmacological treatments for LR-MDS. Outcomes of interest were haematological improvement-erythroid (HI-E), red blood cell transfusion independence (RBC-TI), haematological improvement-platelet (HI-P), and adverse events (AEs).

Results

We included 20 trials (2,877 participants), of which 17 trials (2,670 participants) contributed to connected treatment networks. For HI-E, luspatercept and ESA-based regimens were associated with higher rates. Lenalidomide-containing regimens showed favourable RBC-TI outcomes, including lenalidomide plus ESA, lenalidomide with or without ESA and/or G-CSF, and lenalidomide monotherapy. For HI-P, eltrombopag and romiplostim showed potential benefits. Safety profiles differed across treatments: CC-486 and imetelstat were associated with higher odds of neutropenia and gastrointestinal toxicity, whereas luspatercept was associated with increased fatigue and AEs.

Conclusion

Comparative treatment benefit in LR-MDS differs by clinical endpoint. These findings support an individualised, goal-directed treatment approach rather than a single universally superior therapy.

Systematic review registration

https://www.crd.york.ac.uk/prospero/, identifier CRD420251184384.

records.title: Balanced crystalloids vs. 0.9% saline in pediatric diabetic ketoacidosis: a systematic review and meta-analysis of randomized controlled trials.

content.title: Balanced crystalloids vs. 0.9% saline in pediatric diabetic ketoacidosis: a systematic review and meta-analysis of randomized controlled trials.
content.abstract:
Background

Fluid resuscitation is a cornerstone in the management of pediatric diabetic ketoacidosis (DKA). While 0.9% normal saline (NS) remains the conventional first-line fluid, concerns regarding its high chloride content and potential to induce hyperchloremic metabolic acidosis have led to increasing interest in balanced crystalloids. However, evidence comparing both strategies in pediatric populations remains limited and inconsistent.

Methods

Five databases were searched from inception to 27 April 2026. The primary outcomes were time to resolution of DKA and incidence of new-onset acute kidney injury (AKI). Secondary outcomes included hospital and PICU length of stay, electrolyte disturbances, and major complications. Random-effects models were used. Risk of bias was assessed using the Cochrane RoB 2 tool, and certainty of evidence was evaluated using GRADE.

Results

Five RCTs involving 320 patients were included. A modest but statistically significant decrease in the time to DKA resolution (MD: -1.60 h, 95% CI: -3.07 to -0.13) was associated with balanced crystalloids. Current evidence is insufficient to determine the effect of fluid choice on new-onset AKI due to substantial statistical uncertainty (RR: 0.55, 95% CI: 0.17-1.82; p = 0.325). No significant differences were observed in the other secondary outcomes; however, balanced crystalloids were associated with a lower incidence of hypokalemia (RR: 0.66, 95% CI: 0.46-0.93) and hyperchloremia (RR: 0.40, 95% CI: 0.21-0.78).

Conclusion

Modest benefits in biochemical outcomes were associated with balanced crystalloids. However, due to the small evidence base and low certainty of evidence, it remains unclear if these advantages translate into improvements in clinically important outcomes, particularly rare complications such as cerebral edema and need for mechanical ventilation or inotropic support. Current evidence remains insufficient to support a transition from NS to balanced crystalloids as the initial fluid in pediatric DKA. Further large, multicenter RCTs are needed to better determine the clinical role of balanced crystalloids in this setting.

Systematic review registration

https://www.crd.york.ac.uk/PROSPERO/view/CRD420261387598, identifier CRD420261387598.

records.title: Efficacy and safety of different antithrombotic treatment regimens in patients undergoing transcatheter mitral valve repair and atrial fibrillation; A meta-analysis and systematic review.

content.title: Efficacy and safety of different antithrombotic treatment regimens in patients undergoing transcatheter mitral valve repair and atrial fibrillation; A meta-analysis and systematic review.
content.abstract:
Background

Optimal antithrombotic therapy following transcatheter mitral valve repair (TMVR/TEER) in patients with atrial fibrillation remains uncertain, with substantial practice variation and reliance on nonrandomized data.

Methods

We performed a systematic review and network meta-analysis of observational studies evaluating antithrombotic strategies after TMVR/TEER with atrial fibrillation. Antithrombotic regimens were harmonized into two main categories: oral anticoagulation [OAC; including vitamin K antagonists [VKAs] and direct oral anticoagulants [DOACs]] and antiplatelet therapy (APT; including aspirin or clopidogrel, alone or in combination). Outcomes of interest were ischemic stroke, major bleeding, and all-cause mortality. Pairwise and network random-effects models were applied to derive odds ratios (ORs) with 95% confidence intervals (CIs).

Results

Four multicenter observational cohorts (n = 2,098) were included. Across comparisons, OAC strategies demonstrated a favorable profile compared with APT for bleeding risk reduction, while DOACs showed heterogeneous results depending on comparator drug and study region (phenprocoumon in Europe vs. warfarin in the U.S.). Mortality findings consistently favored OAC (particularly DOACs) potential benefits over APT. For stroke, OAC (phenprocoumon) showed better ischemic prevention, indicating more effectiveness in minimizing stroke risk compared with APT. Network geometry was limited, with most contrasts informed by only one or two studies.

Conclusions

In patients undergoing TMVR/TEER with atrial fibrillation, OAC strategies appeared to be associated with lower bleeding risk and potentially favorable mortality outcomes compared with antiplatelet therapy. However, conclusions regarding comparative efficacy, particularly for stroke prevention, should be interpreted cautiously due to the limited number of studies and the observational nature of the available evidence. Thus, the evidence base remains limited by observational design, heterogeneous comparators, and inconsistent outcome definitions. Randomized trials are urgently needed to guide antithrombotic management in this high-risk population.

records.title: Early predictive value of prediction models for mortality after transcatheter aortic valve replacement: a systematic review and meta-analysis.

content.title: Early predictive value of prediction models for mortality after transcatheter aortic valve replacement: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
content.abstract:
Background

Transcatheter aortic valve replacement (TAVR) is increasingly used due to the rising incidence of aortic stenosis (AS). Early identification of mortality risk after TAVR is challenging. Although various prediction models have been developed, no systematic review has evaluated their effectiveness in predicting mortality risk. Therefore, this study aimed to systematically evaluate the performance of models for early prediction of mortality risk after TAVR, so as to provide evidence-based support for the future development or updating of risk assessment tools.

Methods

Databases (PubMed, Web of Science, Embase, and Cochrane Library) were systematically searched for studies on tools for predicting the risk of mortality after TAVR, up to June 2024. PROBAST was used to assess the risk of bias in the included studies. A subgroup analysis was conducted based on different time points.

Results

This systematic review included 36 studies with 272,390 patients receiving TAVR and 6 major scoring tools encompassing 23 new machine learning models. The meta-analysis showed that the concordance index (C-index) was 0.610 (95% CI: 0.588-0.632) for European System for Cardiac Operative Risk Evaluation I (EuroSCORE I), 0.615 (95% CI: 0.588-0.643) for EuroSCORE II, 0.578 (95% CI: 0.531-0.625) for French Aortic National CoreValve and Edwards II (France II), 0.594 (95% CI: 0.554-0.633) for the OBSERVANT score, 0.648 (95% CI: 0.622-0.674) for the Society of Thoracic Surgeons (STS) risk model, 0.632 (95% CI: 0.616-0.648) for the American College of Cardiology Transcatheter Valve Therapy (ACC TVT) risk model, and 0.705 (95% CI: 0.677-0.733) for summarized machine learning models.

Conclusion

Determining the predictive performance of current established risk assessment tools for predicting the risk of modality after TAVR is challenging. Machine learning models seem to be more effective. Therefore, future research should include more subjects to develop more accurate models.

Systematic review registration

https://www.crd.york.ac.uk/PROSPERO/, identifier CRD42023485237.

records.title: Accuracy of deep learning in the detection of carotid calcifications on cone-beam computed tomography: A systematic review.

content.title: Accuracy of deep learning in the detection of carotid calcifications on cone-beam computed tomography: A systematic review.
content.abstract:
Purpose

This systematic review aimed to describe the diagnostic performance of AI-based models in identifying carotid calcifications using cone-beam computed tomography (CBCT) images.

Materials and methods

A comprehensive search was conducted in the PubMed/MEDLINE, Embase, IEEE Xplore, SciELO, and LILACS databases to identify relevant studies published up to 2025 that evaluated the diagnostic accuracy of artificial intelligence or deep learning systems in detecting carotid artery calcifications using CBCT. Grey literature sources were systematically searched. A qualitative synthesis was conducted for the included studies, followed by a diagnostic accuracy meta-analysis using sensitivity and specificity data. Analyses were performed using bivariate random-effects models (Diagnostic Random-Effects Model). Heterogeneity among studies was assessed using Cochran's Q test, the I2 index, Tau2 statistic, and the corresponding P-value.

Results

A total of 529 records were identified. No additional studies were retrieved from the grey literature. Application of inclusion and exclusion criteria resulted in the selection of four studies for qualitative synthesis.

Conclusion

Despite variations in convolutional neural network (CNN) model architectures, all studies demonstrated that deep learning algorithms applied to CBCT achieve high performance levels in detecting carotid calcifications. The meta-analysis demonstrated that CNN-based models have high diagnostic potential for detecting carotid artery calcifications on CBCT. Although CBCT does not replace gold-standard diagnostic modalities, its use may represent a supportive tool for early screening and clinical referral. The expansion of datasets and the standardization of image acquisition protocols and quality are recommended.

records.title: AI-microbial hybrid biosensors: the next generation of intelligent detection systems.

content.title: AI-microbial hybrid biosensors: the next generation of intelligent detection systems.
content.abstract: The convergence of artificial intelligence (AI) and microbial biosensor technology is transforming pathogen detection, environmental surveillance, antimicrobial resistance (AMR) profiling, and precision diagnostics. Microbial biosensors exploit the specificity of living microorganisms, but signal variability, scalability limits, and interpretive challenges have constrained clinical adoption. Integration of machine learning (ML) and deep neural networks (DNNs) now enables adaptive, high-performance sensing systems. Applied to multi-sensor datasets-such as electrochemical impedance, Raman spectroscopy, and hyperspectral microscopy-convolutional neural networks (CNNs) and ensemble models achieve bacterial classification accuracies of 95-99%, while markedly reducing diagnostic turnaround times and enabling continuous surveillance. Despite rapid progress, the field remains fragmented, lacking a unified synthesis of system architectures, computational strategies, translational barriers, and regulatory considerations. This narrative review provides an integrative analysis of AI-microbial hybrid biosensors, covering biorecognition principles, AI integration approaches, system designs, clinical and environmental applications, performance metrics, and key challenges. It also highlights emerging directions, including synthetic biology, CRISPR-enabled sensing, and edge computing. By consolidating these dimensions, this review positions AI-microbial hybrid biosensors as a next-generation platform for real-time pathogen detection and adaptive biosurveillance. Literature was identified through systematic searches of Google Scholar, PubMed, Web of Science, Scopus, and IEEE Xplore (2000-2026), supplemented by manual reference screening.

records.title: Risk factors associated with postoperative lymphocele in patients with gynecological malignant tumors: a systematic review and meta-analysis.

content.title: Risk factors associated with postoperative lymphocele in patients with gynecological malignant tumors: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
content.abstract:
Background

Pelvic lymphoceles are a common complication after lymph node dissection for gynecological malignancies, with severe cases leading to significant morbidity and delays in adjuvant therapy. This meta-analysis aims to identify risk factors for postoperative lymphoceles and provide evidence for clinical prevention and management.

Methods

A systematic search was performed across eight databases (CNKI, Wanfang, VIP, CBM, Web of Science, PubMed, Cochrane Library, Embase) from inception to August 15, 2025, to include cohort and case-control studies. Two investigators independently screened studies and extracted data. Methodological quality was assessed using the Newcastle-Ottawa Scale, and statistical analyses were conducted with STATA 18.0. Meta-analysis employed fixed- or random-effects models, with heterogeneity evaluated by the I² statistic. The study was registered in PROSPERO (CRD420251053680).

Results

64 studies involving 15,739 patients were included. The pooled incidence of postoperative lymphocele was 30.18%. Moderate to high between-study heterogeneity was detected for most outcomes. Key significant risk factors were as follows: age >50 years (OR = 1.21, 95%CI: 1.02-1.42), BMI ≥24 kg/m² (OR = 1.45, 95%CI: 1.10-1.93), diabetes mellitus (OR = 1.30, 95%CI: 1.11-1.52), laparotomy (OR = 2.76, 95%CI: 2.12-3.58), resection of >20 lymph nodes (OR = 2.75, 95%CI: 2.16-3.51), pelvic and para-aortic lymphadenectomy (OR = 1.86, 95%CI: 1.42-2.43), omentectomy (OR = 1.56, 95%CI: 1.18-2.07), retroperitoneal closure (OR = 2.44, 95%CI: 1.67-3.57), monopolar electrosurgery (OR = 2.48, 95%CI: 1.75-3.51), prolonged operation time (>3h) (OR = 1.56, 95%CI: 1.10-2.21), 24h drainage >100 ml (OR = 1.61, 95%CI: 1.10-2.36), prolonged drainage (>3d) (OR = 1.60, 95%CI: 1.03-2.46), transvaginal drainage (OR = 2.90, 95%CI: 1.92-4.40), ovarian cancer (OR = 1.69, 95%CI: 1.21-2.36), lymphovascular invasion (OR = 1.25, 95%CI: 1.03-1.52), deep myometrial invasion (OR = 1.89, 95%CI: 1.25-2.87), lymph node positivity (OR = 1.59, 95%CI: 1.26-2.00), anemia (OR = 1.20, 95%CI: 1.02-1.40), hypoalbuminemia (OR = 1.58, 95%CI: 1.07-2.34), postoperative chemotherapy (OR = 1.85, 95%CI: 1.29-2.65), and concurrent chemoradiotherapy (OR = 2.49, 95%CI: 1.68-3.69). Advanced FIGO stage was also significant.

Conclusions

Clinicians can stratify lymphocele risk by integrating preoperative features, surgical procedures, tumor pathology, nutritional status, and adjuvant therapy to guide individualized management. Intraoperatively, rational planning, limited lymphadenectomy, retroperitoneal preservation, and standardized use of energy devices are recommended. Postoperatively, optimized drainage and correction of nutritional disorders reduce lymphocele risk. Given heterogeneity in some risk factors and predominance of single-center retrospective studies, well-designed prospective studies with unified criteria are needed to validate and refine prevention strategies.

Systematic review registration

https://www.crd.york.ac.uk/prospero/, identifier PROSPERO (CRD420251053680).

records.title: Intelligent technology-driven diabetes prevention and control: From informatization management to artificial intelligence.

content.title: Intelligent technology-driven diabetes prevention and control: From informatization management to artificial intelligence.
content.abstract: The escalating prevalence of diabetes, along with its complications and mortality risks, imposes a substantial disease burden worldwide. The current suboptimal medical conditions and poor self-management among diabetic patients have exacerbated the deterioration of diabetes globally, particularly in economically underdeveloped countries. However, this situation may now be approaching a turning point. With the constantly advancement of intelligent technologies, the widespread adoption of information management systems and the rise of artificial intelligence have made it possible to enhance the efficiency of diabetes treatment and reduce management costs. Therefore, we have reviewed the relevant literature and conducted a narrative review following the guidance of the Scale for the Assessment of Narrative Review Articles (SANRA). The present paper provides a narrative review of research advances from information management to artificial intelligence in the field of diabetes treatment and management, while also discussing the opportunities and challenges in clinical translation and application. The present review offers a conceptual framework to inform future research and development in intelligent diabetes care.

records.title: Optimal drain position after evacuation of chronic subdural hematomas: a systematic review and network meta-analysis.

content.title: Optimal drain position after evacuation of chronic subdural hematomas: a systematic review and network meta-analysis.
content.abstract:
Background

Chronic subdural hematoma (CSDH) is one of the most prevalent diseases encountered in neurosurgery. At present, burr-hole hematoma drainage has been established as the standard surgical intervention for CSDH, effectively reducing the risk of postoperative recurrence. The current study employed systematic review and network meta-analysis (NMA) to assess the impact of drain placement in three different anatomical locations-subdural drain (SDD), subperiosteal drain (SPD), and subgaleal drain (SGD)-on treatment outcomes.

Methods

A search was conducted across PubMed, Embase, Cochrane Library, and Web of Science up to February 14, 2026. The Newcastle-Ottawa Scale was used to assess the risk of bias. R (v4.4.0) and Stata18 were used for the NMA.

Results

This NMA included 14 articles comprising 4,161 patients. The drainage locations evaluated were SDD, SPD, and SGD. Pooled results were analyzed based on two classification systems: Classification I (anatomical location) and Classification II (anatomical location + technique). (1) Recurrence rate: Classification I: According to the league table, SGD was associated with a significantly lower recurrence rate versus No_drain [risk ratio (RR) = 0.43, 95% credible interval (CrI): 0.20-0.96]. Based on the surface under the cumulative ranking curve (SUCRA), SGD (78.25%) ranked as the best intervention. Classification II: According to the league table, subgaleal active drainage (SGD_a) was significantly associated with recurrence versus No_drain (RR = 0.26, 95% CrI: 0.10-0.75), and also ranked highest in SUCRA (79.83%). (2) Mortality: Classification I: SGD was associated with reduced mortality (SUCRA = 72.64%). Classification II: subdural irrigation drainage (SDD_irr) showed the best efficacy in reducing mortality (SUCRA = 63.85%).

Conclusion

SGD_a and SDD_irr exhibit significant potential in reducing recurrence rates and mortality, respectively, in the management of CSDH. However, due to the physiological conditions and disease features of old and high-risk populations, careful assessment is necessary when selecting treatment approaches in clinical practice. Further studies should be conducted to clarify the actual efficacy of these two treatment modalities.

Systematic review registration

This study is a systematic review and network meta-analysis and has been registered in the PROSPERO database. Registration ID: CRD42024587692. Official URL: https://www.crd.york.ac.uk/prospero/display_record.php?RecordID=587692.

records.title: Evidence-Based Performance of Artificial Intelligence in Dental Age Assessment: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis Using Orthopantomograms

content.title: Evidence-Based Performance of Artificial Intelligence in Dental Age Assessment: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis Using Orthopantomograms
content.abstract:
Background: Chronological age estimation based on biological markers plays a crucial role in forensic, legal, and clinical contexts. Among available methods, dental age assessment (DAA) using orthopantomograms (OPGs) is considered one of the most accurate approaches. However, conventional DAA methods rely on expert interpretation, introducing subjectivity and limiting reproducibility. In recent years, artificial intelligence (AI) has emerged as a promising solution to overcome these limitations. This systematic review with meta-analysis aimed to evaluate the performance of AI-based models for dental age assessment using OPGs.

Methods:

The review protocol followed PRISMA guidelines and was registered in PROSPERO. A total of 27 studies, published between 2020 and 2025, were included, encompassing a wide range of machine learning and deep learning approaches, predominantly convolutional neural networks (CNNs).

Results:

For chronological age estimation, the pooled root mean squared error (RMSE) was 1.76 years, indicating that AI models can predict age with an average deviation of less than two years from true chronological age. The pooled coefficient of determination (R²) was 0.92, reflecting strong agreement and high explanatory power between predicted and actual ages. In classification tasks related to legal age thresholds, AI models demonstrated high discriminatory performance, with an overall area under the curve (AUC) exceeding 0.90 and a high diagnostic odds ratio (DOR). Hierarchical summary receiver operator characteristic analyses (HSROC) revealed high pooled sensitivity and specificity, with a slightly stronger ability to correctly classify individuals below the legal threshold. Network meta-analyses consistently ranked human expert assessments lower than AI-based models, especially CNN architectures such as EfficientNet, ResNet, and VGG16, although differences were not statistically significant.

Conclusions:
